rounds.proof_sketch: With num_features=64, update_blocks=(64+255)/256=1. In 1D launch <<<1,256>>>, blockIdx.x=0 and blockIdx.y=0 (default). Both original (blockIdx.x*256+threadIdx.x) and mutated (blockIdx.y*256+threadIdx.x) compute idx=threadIdx.x. The mutation would only matter if num_features>256, requiring multiple blocks where blockIdx.x>0.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes blockIdx.x to blockIdx.y in the update_running_stats_kernel index calculation. However, with the fixed num_features=64, only one block is launched (update_blocks=1), so blockIdx.x is always 0. Since this is a 1D grid launch (only x-dimension specified), blockIdx.y defaults to 0 as well. Both versions therefore compute identical index values: idx = 0 * 256 + threadIdx.x = threadIdx.x. The mutation would produce different behavior only if num_features exceeded 256, requiring multiple blocks where blockIdx.x would be non-zero for subsequent blocks.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed configuration. Would require num_features > 256 to have multiple blocks where blockIdx.x differs from blockIdx.y.
rounds.recommendations: When testing kernels with dimension-based indexing mutations, ensure test configurations exercise multi-block scenarios. For this kernel, testing with num_features > 256 would expose the bug. Consider adding assertions to validate that expected index ranges are covered across all launched blocks.
